title: Identical cell rules yield diverse behaviors through different configurations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Identical cell rules yield diverse behaviors through different configurations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Even though every cell of a cellular automaton follows the same rule, different configurations of cell colors can collectively produce many different kinds of behavior, such as regular backgrounds and distinct localized structures.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: even though individual cells follow the same rule, different configurations of cells with different sequences of colors can together produce all sorts of different kinds of behavior.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 2, “The Crucial Experiment”; section “The Need for a New Intuition” (from p. 39), p. 39. Scope: cellular automata, exemplified by rule 110

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch02-09: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The existential statement is directly demonstrated by reproducible configurations under rule 110 and other rules. Different periodic domains and localized structures can be identified with objective spatiotemporal signatures.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Run one fixed cellular-automaton rule from multiple configurations and classify resulting backgrounds, particles, and interactions. Distinct reproducible collective behaviors under the identical local rule confirm the existence claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Behavioral categories require modest classification choices.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is that one shared cell rule plus different finite configurations yields qualitatively different collective behavior. Rule 110's periodic ether and its distinct gliders are a direct witness, regenerated by any elementary-automaton simulator and catalogued in the universality proof. The example's scope is fully covered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In one cellular automaton, isolate a regular background and at least two localized structures with different velocities or periods, each a finite configuration evolving under the same cell rule. Finding those configurations confirms the claim; a rule in which every finite configuration produces only one kind of behavior would refute the general reading, and rule 110 is the stated example.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Under the single local rule of elementary cellular automaton rule 110, random initial configurations settle into one dominant periodic background (the 'ether') while other finite configurations embedded in it evolve as persistent localized structures with several distinct, exactly periodic signatures (different velocities), so one rule produces qualitatively different kinds of collective behavior.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: analysis.py enumerates all 16384 configurations of a 14-cell ring under rule 110 and finds those that return to a rotation of themselves after 7 steps; the only non-uniform orbit (14 rotations of 00010011011111, shift 0 after 7 steps, basin 51.5% of ring states) is the ether. Twenty random initial conditions on a 700-cell ring are run for 3000 steps; a cell is 'background' when its 14-cell window equals one of the ether's window codes. Non-background cells are clustered (gap <= 3), clusters are linked across steps (centre moves <= 6 cells), and each track of >= 300 steps is tested for exact periodicity (window at t equals window at t+p shifted by s for 5 consecutive periods, p <= 60). Distinct rational velocities s/p differing by > 0.05 are counted.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. (A) Background: there is a configuration on a 14-cell ring that rule 110 maps, after 7 steps, onto a rotation of itself (a spatially 14-periodic, temporally 7-periodic background), and in 20 independent random-initial-condition runs (density 0.5, cyclic lattice of 700 cells, 3000 steps) the mean fraction of cells whose 14-cell neighbourhood matches that background (any phase) over steps 1000-3000 is at least 0.50. (B) Structures: across the same runs, tracks of non-background cells that persist for at least 300 steps and are exactly periodic (the window around the track at time t equals the window at time t+p shifted by s cells, for 5 consecutive periods) exist with at least 3 distinct velocities s/p (pairwise differing by more than 0.05 cells/step). Both (A) and (B) must hold for 'supports'.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if no 7-step periodic 14-cell background exists or the mean background fraction is below 0.25, or if fewer than 2 distinct exactly periodic localized-structure velocities are found across all runs. Anything between (background fraction 0.25-0.50, or exactly 2 velocities) is 'mixed'.

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: exact (deterministic computation); background fraction range over runs 0.619-0.886

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Wolfram's statement is read as an existence claim about rule 110 (his stated example): the same cell rule, applied to different local configurations, yields (i) a regular periodic background and (ii) several distinct localized structures. 'Regular background' is operationalized as a spatially and temporally periodic configuration; 'localized structure' as a bounded cluster of non-background cells that persists and is exactly periodic up to a shift, so that its velocity s/p is a rational number. Distinct velocities are taken as evidence of 'different kinds of behavior'. No reinterpretation beyond this is needed; the test is computational and the 'dataset' is generated by analysis.py.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value: Elementary cellular automaton rule 110, random initial conditions (generated by analysis.py)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Background matching uses a 14-cell window, so cells within 13 cells of a structure are flagged as non-background; the 0.80 background fraction is therefore a lower bound.

Tracks that collide or split are cut, so the 143 periodic tracks are a sample, not a census, of structures; the velocities found (2/3, -1/2, 0, 1/5, -4/15, -1/3, -1/9) coincide with Cook's gliders A, B, C, D, E, G, F but that catalogue was not used in the detection.

The test covers rule 110 (Wolfram's stated example); the claim's general wording about cellular automata is supported only by this witness.
